questions.stem: In the routine titration trial exercise below, a student notes the observed value. To estimate a mean within 1.19 units at about 95 percent confidence, with a preliminary standard deviation of 3.12, approximately how many samples are needed using z = 1.96?

leaves out the critical z value

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: determine required sample size for a target confidence interval
questions.stem: In the routine spectrophotometric assay exercise below, a student obtains the reported result. To estimate a mean within 0.96 units at about 95 percent confidence, with a preliminary standard deviation of 2.88, how many samples are needed, approximately using z = 1.96?

options.misconception: omits the square required by the sample-size formula
leaves out the critical z value
multiplies by the margin of error instead of dividing

questions.explanation: Rearranging the confidence-interval margin gives sample size n equals z times s over the desired margin, all squared. The square is essential because the margin shrinks with the square root of n. Omitting z or the square understates the needed sample count.
